$comment: The KernelSU late-load build this target would pair with. Written ahead of
the build that proves it: quest3 is not in src/targets.json, so nothing
reads this file yet -- generate_feed.py only sees a target the feed knows
about. It is here because these are properties of the target rather than
of whoever builds it, and because two of them are not guesses.
MEASURED on the device (5.10.240-g55be3759aea4, build 52345320035400520):
CONFIG_MODULES=y, CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD=y and CONFIG_MODULE_SIG is NOT
set -- an unsigned module is loadable. CONFIG_MODVERSIONS=y, which the
build already answers by emptying Module.symvers so __versions comes out
zero-length and ksud resolves the undefined symbols from /proc/kallsyms
before init_module; that is how every target here loads, not something
particular to this one.
A late-load driven from an adb shell reaches init_module on this device.
Tried with the android14-6.1 module from another target, deliberately, to
find out where it would stop: vermagic and the version check both passed
and it failed on symbol names alone --
kernelsu: no symbol version for module_layout
kernelsu: Unknown symbol _printk (err -2)
kernelsu: Unknown symbol kmalloc_trace (err -2)
kernelsu: Unknown symbol __alloc_pages (err -2)
... 10 in total
all of which are the 6.x spellings of things 5.10 calls something else
(printk, kmem_cache_alloc_trace, __alloc_pages_nodemask). So the gate is
a module built for the right series, and nothing further down.
'kmi' is android12-5.10 because the audit says so, not because of the
ship date. Built from that DDK and checked against a Module.symvers
extracted from this kernel:
android14-6.1 (another target's module)   10 MISSING_SYMBOL
android12-5.10, DDK config as shipped      1 MISSING_SYMBOL
android12-5.10, config aligned (below)     0 MISSING_SYMBOL
python3 src/kernelsu/tools/extract_target_symvers.py <vmlinux> syms
python3 src/kernelsu/tools/audit_module_against_target.py <ko> <vmlinux> syms
MISSING_SYMBOL is the fatal class -- a name the kernel does not have at
all, which is what the 6.1 module failed on and what kallsyms resolution
cannot rescue. MISSING_EXPORT is not: those are resolved from kallsyms,
and 48 of them are. The tool is trustworthy here: run against the
android14-6.1 module it named exactly the ten symbols the device's own
dmesg did.
STILL NOT ANSWERED, and it is not a symbol question. This is not a GKI
kernel -- Meta builds its own -- so the DDK's gki_defconfig is an
approximation of it, and the differences move structures the module reads.
Comparing only the options that guard task_struct fields leaves five:
KASAN / KASAN_HW_TAGS   DDK yes, device no  -> task_struct.kasan_depth
PREEMPT_NOTIFIERS       DDK yes, device no  -> task_struct.preempt_notifiers
TASK_DELAY_ACCT         DDK yes, device no  -> task_struct.delays
UBSAN_TRAP              DDK yes, device no  -> traps compiled into the module
STACKPROTECTOR_PER_TASK device yes, DDK no  -> codegen only, layout unaffected
The first four have to come off the DDK config before the build; the fifth
cannot go on (the DDK's clang-12 rejects -mstack-protector-guard=sysreg,
which the device's clang-14 build uses) and does not need to. There is no
field in this file for that yet: it is done by hand, and the porting notes
carry the procedure.
The aligned module resolves every symbol and still reboots the device
when ksud loads it -- three runs, every one of them. The reboot records
nothing: sys.boot.reason is 'reboot', this kernel has no
CONFIG_PSTORE_RAM, and a logcat capture armed on /data came back 0 bytes,
so not even userspace's buffered writes survive it. Abrupt enough to be a
kernel crash rather than a restart.
What is ruled out: a plain insmod of the same module is refused
harmlessly on the 48 unexported symbols, so format, vermagic and the
version check all pass and the crash is after ksud resolves those from
kallsyms. kptr_restrict is not it either -- this device ships 2, which
hides every kallsyms address from root as well, and the helper now sets 0
across the load; the reboot survived that fix.
What is left is that the DDK is an approximation. GKI's KMI is stable for
a kernel built with its config, and Meta's is not: the five differences
above are the ones that guard task_struct fields, but nothing says they
are the only ones that matter to code this module compiles inline.
Answering it properly wants Meta's kernel source for this build rather
than more attempts against a generic DDK.
'id' is quest3 rather than a shared one: no other target loads this module.
'patchSets' is empty -- this device has no vendor hardening the sets exist
for -- and 'config' goes with a set, so it is empty too.
